commands.review_summary:
The PR wires `models.providers.runway.request` into Runway video submit request resolution and adds a regression test for configured headers, private-network allowance, and dispatcher policy on the create call.

PR surface: Source +3, Tests +82. Total +85 across 2 files.

Reproducibility: yes. Source inspection of current main shows Runway video generation does not pass `models.providers.runway.request` into the HTTP resolver, and PR-head source shows the remaining poll/download policy gap.
commands.review_followup: - [P2] A narrow automated repair can pass the resolved policy into Runway poll/download and add focused regression coverage.

target.title: fix(runway): apply configured request policy to video generation requests
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Runway video generation currently ignores `models.providers.runway.request` overrides (headers, allowPrivateNetwork, dispatcherPolicy). Users who configure a request policy for Runway see it applied to chat/completion providers but not to video generation, so private-network access, custom headers, and dispatcher routing are dropped on the floor.

## Why This Change Was Made

Mirror the pattern already used by `openai`, `pixverse`, `google` image generation, and Alix-007's recent DashScope/MiniMax/OpenRouter video request-policy PRs: pass `sanitizeConfiguredModelProviderRequest(providerConfig?.request)` into `resolveProviderHttpRequestConfig` so the configured transport overrides flow into the create request.

## Changes

- `extensions/runway/video-generation-provider.ts`
  - Import `sanitizeConfiguredModelProviderRequest`.
  - Read `req.cfg?.models?.providers?.runway`.
  - Forward the sanitized request policy to `resolveProviderHttpRequestConfig`.
- `extensions/runway/video-generation-provider.test.ts`
  - Add regression test asserting that configured headers, `allowPrivateNetwork`, and `dispatcherPolicy` reach `postJsonRequest`.
  - Fix test type errors caught by `check-test-types`.

## Intentionally Out of Scope

- Poll/download stages continue to use the headers resolved at create time; this change does not refactor them onto `fetchWithTimeoutGuarded`, matching the minimal scope of the existing video request-policy PRs.
- No new helper or shared abstraction is introduced.

## Evidence

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/runway/video-generation-provider.test.ts
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/extensions-test.tsbuildinfo
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.extensions.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/extensions.tsbuildinfo
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.extensions.json extensions/runway/video-generation-provider.ts extensions/runway/video-generation-provider.test.ts
```

- Vitest: 10/10 passing.
- `tsgo` (source + test): no type errors.
- `oxlint`: clean.

Real behavior proof against a local Runway-compatible endpoint, showing the configured `X-Runway-Policy` header is sent and private-network access is allowed:

```
[proof] local Runway-compatible endpoint at http://127.0.0.1:37479
[server] POST /v1/text_to_video
[server] Authorization: Bearer dummy-runway-key
[server] X-Runway-Policy: runway-policy
[server] GET /v1/tasks/task-proof
[server] GET /video.mp4
[proof] generated video count: 1
[proof] video MIME type: video/mp4
[proof] done
```
